title: Interval list intersections
statement: A and B are each sorted lists of disjoint closed intervals. Return their intersection as a sorted list of closed intervals.
hints: Two intervals overlap in [max(starts), min(ends)] when that is non-empty.
Advance whichever interval ends first: it can't intersect anything further in the other list.

solution.explanation: Two pointers, like merging sorted lists. The overlap of two intervals is [max start, min end]. The interval that ends first is finished, because every later interval in the other list starts after the current one, so drop it. The same "advance the one that ends first" step is the core of interval merging, meeting-time matching and calendar availability problems.
